content:
Since we are thinking about eLpNorm refactors, I had one question about the name. I thought eLpNorm was like edist: we add an e in front so that we can later make a second declaration lpNorm/LpNorm that takes values into ℝ instead of ℝ≥0∞. I now think that such an ℝ-valued norm is not useful to have.

Does this mean we should get rid of the e-prefix of the name? One possible counterargument is that even if we never define the real-valued version, the e reminds us that this takes values in ENNReal.
Indeed I added the e because I was about to add nnLpNorm, but @Sébastien Gouëzel stopped me in #23881
Why do you think we should not have docs#MeasureTheory.lpNorm ?
Oh wait, we do have lpNorm? I did not realize that!
6 messages were moved here from #mathlib4 > eLpNorm junk value by Floris van Doorn.

I guess I never really needed it, and pushed all computations to ENNReal. I guess if you are working with complex numbers/vector spaces over ℝ and want to take the scalar product of the L^p-norm of something with a vector, this might be useful. And if you write (eLpNorm f μ p).toReal enough, I can imagine a new definition can be useful. Is it used frequently in APAP?

That at least answers my original question negatively.
Yes, precisely. A common step in APAP is to rewrite the L^2n norm to the power of 2n as a sum of exponentials in the complex numbers
